Pool membership is checked against immutable factory and callback caller against transient expected pool plus factory. Payer is msg.sender on initial funding and router on intermediate hops. Output goes to caller-specified recipient. tokenIn/tokenOut and adjacent path token addresses are NOT checked against pool token immutables: wrong choices can revert, send an unexpected token or strand publicly sweepable router balances.

Amounts are raw token units, inputs uint128 constrained to signed int128 range. Every swap enforces deadline and final minimum output or maximum input; single-hop additionally applies Q64.64 marginal price limit (0 for zeroForOne open, uint128.max for opposite open). Single exact input can partially fill at its price bound. Multihop arrays must align and contain 1..256 pools; directions are bitmap bits, no per-hop price limits. Exact-output traverses pools backward through fixed internal callbacks.

extensionData is forwarded only through the selected factory pool swap to that pool's configured extension, not interpreted as arbitrary router executor calldata. Pool pricing, fees, oracle freshness, permissions, pause state and mutable configured financial hooks remain material dependencies; individual pool/hook runtime identity and configuration are not attested here.

Payable swaps may wrap native currency for the immutable wrapped-native input before transferring any remaining input from msg.sender. Excess or unspent native currency can remain on the router and is publicly refundable; ERC20-only calls should send zero native value. Refund/unwrap/sweep helpers are not admitted, so this scope does not promise native refund or full workflow.

Router-funded swaps retain unused input for subsequent steps; append a sweep or unwrap to collect leftovers.

returns.amountSpent: Net funded input not returned to the router, floored at zero.

sequence((bytes,uint8,uint8)[]).details: Delegatecalls this router, preserving caller and value. STOP leaves later results empty and statuses NOT_EXECUTED;      REVERT rolls back all steps with SequenceFailed. Both returned and error arrays retain calls.length.      Unexecuted steps have empty results and NOT_EXECUTED status. Each result is capped at 4096 bytes.      A step can be an encoded multicall, so a route and its cleanup succeed or roll back together. A failed step      is rolled back, so msg.value stays available to the next one. limitations: Static source/ABI and deployment metadata only: not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Ethereum current v1 MetricOmmSimpleRouter only; nonproxy. Source reports Sourcify runtimeMatch=match and creationMatch=match, not exact_match. Registered Metric pool swaps only; externalSwap, sequence, multicall, permits, callbacks and public payment/sweep helpers are excluded.

Pool membership is checked against immutable factory and callback caller against transient expected pool plus factory. Payer is msg.sender on initial funding and router on intermediate hops. Output goes to caller-specified recipient. tokenIn/tokenOut and adjacent path token addresses are NOT checked against pool token immutables: wrong choices can revert, send an unexpected token or strand publicly sweepable router balances.

Amounts are raw token units, inputs uint128 constrained to signed int128 range. Every swap enforces deadline and final minimum output or maximum input; single-hop additionally applies Q64.64 marginal price limit (0 for zeroForOne open, uint128.max for opposite open). Single exact input can partially fill at its price bound. Multihop arrays must align and contain 1..256 pools; directions are bitmap bits, no per-hop price limits. Exact-output traverses pools backward through fixed internal callbacks.

extensionData is forwarded only through the selected factory pool swap to that pool's configured extension, not interpreted as arbitrary router executor calldata. Pool pricing, fees, oracle freshness, permissions, pause state and mutable configured financial hooks remain material dependencies; individual pool/hook runtime identity and configuration are not attested here.

Payable swaps may wrap native currency for the immutable wrapped-native input before transferring any remaining input from msg.sender. Excess or unspent native currency can remain on the router and is publicly refundable; ERC20-only calls should send zero native value. Refund/unwrap/sweep helpers are not admitted, so this scope does not promise native refund or full workflow.
